players.name: Márcio Rosa
players.note: The Bulgarian-league keeper who's third in the goalkeeping queue here, which on a first-ever World Cup squad still means a front-row seat to history.

players.name: Vózinha
players.note: At 39 he's the squad's elder statesman and vice-captain, the steady voice who waited his whole career for the islands to finally reach a World Cup.

players.name: C. dos Santos
players.note: Born in the US and once a youth international for the hosts, he switched to his father's Cape Verde and now gets a home World Cup with his MLS club San Diego on the doorstep.

players.name: Diney Borges
players.note: A defender plying his trade in the UAE, one of those quietly-travelled names that make this the most well-stamped passport collection at the tournament.

players.name: Logan Costa
players.note: Born near Paris and once in France's youth ranks, he chose Cape Verde and is now the squad's only man from Europe's top five leagues, anchoring the back line at Villarreal.

players.name: S. Lopes Cabral
players.note: The Dutch-born right-back climbed from German lower divisions to a Benfica move in early 2026, the kind of fast rise that lands you at a debut World Cup at 23.

players.name: Pico
players.note: Dublin-born Roberto Lopes was tracked down through a message online and capped by descent, and now becomes the first active League of Ireland player to grace a World Cup.

players.name: S. Moreira
players.note: Steven Moreira does his defending in MLS with Columbus, so unlike most of his teammates he won't need a map for the long American summer ahead.

players.name: Wagner Pina
players.note: A young full-back earning his keep in Turkey with Trabzonspor, part of the next generation Bubista is folding into this history-making group.

players.name: Kelvin Pires
players.note: His football home is the Finnish league with SJK, about as far from a Group H showdown with Spain as a defender can travel and still get there.

players.name: Stopira
players.note: At 37 he's one of the longest-serving Blue Sharks of all, the sort of loyal old hand who's seen every near-miss and finally gets the payoff.

players.name: Telmo Arcanjo
players.note: A Vitória Guimarães midfielder who adds youthful legs to a side that leans heavily on its veterans, with plenty of room left to grow into the moment.

players.name: Deroy Duarte
players.note: Rotterdam-raised and now at Bulgaria's Ludogorets, he's the younger of two Duarte brothers in this squad, which makes for one very proud household back home.

players.name: L. Duarte
players.note: Laros is the elder Duarte, a former Sparta Rotterdam man now in Hungary, sharing a midfield and a debut World Cup with his little brother Deroy.

players.name: João Paulo
players.note: He patrols the middle for Romania's Oțelul Galați, another of the under-the-radar names whose steady leagues quietly built this remarkable qualifying run.

players.name: Kevin Pina
players.note: Based in Russia with Krasnodar, he's one of the wide runners Bubista can call on to stretch defences that will mostly outrank Cape Verde on paper.

players.name: Jamiro Monteiro
players.note: The Rotterdam-born playmaker spent years lighting up MLS with Philadelphia and San Jose before heading back to the Dutch top flight, and he's the engine in this midfield.

players.name: Yannick Semedo
players.note: Born Jair Semedo Monteiro, this Farense midfielder is a relative latecomer to the cause who timed his arrival perfectly for the islands' big year.

players.name: Garry Rodrigues
players.note: A Rotterdam kid who picked his parents' islands over the Netherlands, he won a Turkish title at Galatasaray and at 35 brings the most glamour to the wing.

players.name: Nuno da Costa
players.note: A French-cup winner with Strasbourg who later had a Nottingham Forest spell, the well-travelled forward now turns out in Istanbul for Başakşehir.

players.name: Jovane Cabral
players.note: Raised in the Sporting academy and once loaned to Lazio, this island-born winger is the rare squad member who actually grew up in Cape Verde rather than the diaspora.

players.name: Willy Semedo
players.note: France-born and now a tidy finisher for Omonia in Cyprus, he's another diaspora pick-up who answered the call to wear the blue.

players.name: Hélio Varela
players.note: At 23 and playing for Maccabi Tel Aviv, he's one of the youngest of the bunch, wearing the symbolic No. 26 shirt for a 26-man trip into the unknown.

players.name: Ryan Mendes
players.note: The captain, 36, is Cape Verde's record scorer and most-capped player, a former Lille man who finally gets to lead the islands out at a World Cup.

players.name: Gilson Benchimol
players.note: A young forward making his way in the Russian league with Akron, handed the No. 9 shirt and the chance to chase the islands' first World Cup goals.

players.name: D. Livramento
players.note: The qualifying campaign's breakout striker, his winner against Cameroon and opener against Eswatini did as much as anyone to drag the islands to a first World Cup.
